claims.text: AI systems increasingly participate in multi-step scientific processes rather than only isolated prediction tasks.
claims.boundary: does not imply full autonomous science is reliable or general

claims.text: Published systems now connect literature/search, hypothesis generation, experiment or computation, analysis and revision in several scientific settings.
claims.boundary: capabilities differ by system and domain; 'connect' does not mean every stage is fully autonomous

claims.text: A-Lab integrates computation, literature-derived knowledge, machine/active learning and robotic experiments for inorganic materials synthesis.
Coscientist uses language models with search, code and experimental automation to design, plan and perform chemistry experiments.
Robin connects literature-based hypothesis generation and data analysis in experimental biology.
The AI Scientist demonstrates an end-to-end computational research pipeline spanning idea generation, experimentation, analysis, writing and self-review.
claims.boundary: the paper's workshop-review result is not treated as proof of general scientific reliability

claims.text: Machine Epistemics is defined here as the proposed study and engineering of warranted machine-mediated scientific-state transitions.
claims.boundary: definition does not establish novelty or field status

claims.text: A machine-epistemic episode is proposed as a bounded object containing problem/criterion, scientific state, obligations, actions, resources, evidence/provenance/dependence, evaluators, observations, history and authority.
claims.boundary: not claimed as a universal ontology

claims.text: A successful software/tool execution need not establish the scientific claim for which its output is later used.
claims.boundary: formal checker outputs can be decisive when the claim/specification relationship is valid

claims.text: Provenance representation can establish lineage/interchange properties without by itself establishing scientific correctness.
claims.boundary: PROV is not designed as a truth criterion

claims.text: Truth-maintenance systems already record reasons for beliefs and revise them after contradictory discoveries.
Model-based diagnosis already formalizes competing explanations for observed system discrepancies and discriminating measurements.
Rational metareasoning already formalizes selection of computational actions under uncertainty and resource bounds.
Performative prediction formalizes settings in which deploying predictions changes the outcomes/distribution being predicted.
Agentic science and verification-first autonomous science are existing adjacent programmes rather than concepts invented by Machine Epistemics.
Machine behaviour was proposed in Nature as an emerging interdisciplinary scientific field concerned with intelligent machines as empirical actors.
The machine-behaviour proposal received a published Nature criticism arguing that cybernetics already covered relevant territory.
Computational social science was framed around new large-scale digital traces and associated methodological/institutional challenges.
Science of science operationalizes a transdisciplinary field through large-scale data on the production of science and searches for universal and domain-specific patterns.
Sustainability Robotics was explicitly advocated in Nature Machine Intelligence as a new discipline organized by three principles and two dimensions.
Network medicine reframed disease using network-level interdependencies and developed organizing principles/applications from that object.
No mature existing field already owns the complete machine-epistemic episode and all proposed composition-level transition decisions.
claims.resolution_test: complete parent-domain and changed-vocabulary demarcation audit; construct information-matched strongest parent composition; seek independent demarcation review

claims.text: Cross-layer decisions such as provenance-to-validity, relation-to-reuse, evidence-to-authority and route-stop-to-scientific-closure recur across materially different sciences.
claims.boundary: published examples motivate recurrence; cross-domain protected tests are still required for a strong field claim

claims.text: The proposed four control problems provide a coherent organizational framework for Machine Epistemics.
claims.resolution_test: blind expert/demarcation review and cross-domain instantiation should test whether the four problems are stable/nonredundant

claims.text: Machine Epistemics can produce formal and empirical research questions concerning observability, justified reachability, transport, dependence, selective reopening, escalation and stopping.
claims.boundary: many individual problems are parent-owned; field-level composition remains unproved

claims.text: A distinct Machine Epistemics field should be rejected if strongest parent compositions reproduce the same protected cross-domain decisions.
Machine Epistemics currently constitutes an established new scientific field.
claims.reason: the manuscript explicitly proposes a provisional field hypothesis; external scientific/community recognition and protected residual evidence are not yet present

claims.text: Nature Machine Intelligence Perspectives are intended for fast-moving/emerging scholarly topics with original forward-looking vision and are peer reviewed.
Nature Machine Intelligence currently requires human accountability for scholarly content and treats AI as support rather than a replacement for scholarly judgment.
The current flagship is publication-ready for Nature Machine Intelligence.
claims.resolution_test: full citation-entailment audit, complete bibliography and contrary literature, conceptual figures, blind review/revision, surface QA, AI-use disclosure, independent demarcation review

note: The CONTRADICTED field-status claim is intentionally retained as a hostile assertion that the manuscript must never imply. A full sentence-by-sentence manuscript atomic audit remains required before any simulated-publication-ready terminal.
